scope: The street-corner Casa de la Independencia Museum in Asunción as seen in the two early published color references. Includes the whitewashed street wings, clay-tile roofs, raised entrance steps, open central garden court, and the gateway on 14 de Mayo. Omits interior exhibits, the separately mapped historic alley and the later recovery of the adjacent former stable lot.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The national cultural authority identifies the Presidente Franco and 14 de Mayo corner and the 1965 museum opening.
The municipal heritage inventory describes two bodies flanking an open garden court, whitewashed brick replacing the original adobe, and a traditional clay tile roof over timber.
The museum describes the residential hall-corridor and five rooms surrounding the open patio.

next: Build the corner gabled wing, raised facade steps, open courtyard and independent 14 de Mayo gateway. Retain the two distinct roof silhouettes in every detail level.
